subject: Book Keeping
preamble: The Book Keeping syllabus is designed to assess the candidates' basic knowledge of business activities and understanding of financial system for the purpose of establishing a business and laying a good foundation for further studies.
aims: knowledge of basic skills required to start a business;
ability to appreciate the rules and functions of book keeping;
ability to apply the basic knowledge and skills in Book Keeping to modern business activities.

papers.title: Objective Questions
papers.details: Forty multiple-choice objective questions, all of which must be answered.

papers.title: Theory and Practice
papers.details: Composite paper consisting of two sections. Section A (Theory): 4 questions, candidates answer 2 (20 marks). Section B (Practice): 5 questions, candidates answer 3 (60 marks).

detailed_syllabus.section_name: Core Book Keeping Concepts & Financial Accounting

topics.title: 1. Introduction to Book Keeping
topics.notes: Meaning, definition, history, nature, importance, and functions of book keeping; career opportunities and beneficiaries; qualities and values of book keepers. Assets and Liabilities: definition, differences, classification, and examples. Business Transactions: meaning, types, and parties involved. Classification of Accounts: personal accounts (debtors and creditors), impersonal accounts (real and nominal). Source Documents: definition, identification, types, and uses.

topics.title: 2. Concepts and Conventions
topics.notes: Definition, identification, and differences between accounting concepts and conventions.

topics.title: 3. Books of Original Entry
topics.notes: Definition, purpose, types, format, uses, and preparation of Books of Original Entry.

topics.title: 4. Ledger and Principles of Double Entry
topics.notes: Ledger: definition, classification, format, uses, and preparation. Principles of Double Entry: meaning, history, rules, and posting double entries.

topics.title: 5. Cash Book
topics.notes: Meaning, purpose, description, differences, and preparation of single column, double column, three column, and petty cash books.

topics.title: 6. Bank Reconciliation Statement
topics.notes: Meaning and purpose; terminologies and banking documents; causes of differences between cash book and bank statement balances.

topics.title: 7. Trial Balance and Errors
topics.notes: Meaning, functions, rules, and preparation of trial balance; meaning, types, and classification of errors; correction of errors and preparation of Suspense Account.

topics.title: 8. Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
topics.notes: Trading Account: definition, purpose, format, preparation, and stock valuation methods (FIFO and LIFO). Profit and Loss Account: definition, purpose, format, and preparation. Balance Sheet: meaning, content, format, and preparation.

topics.title: 9. Adjustments to Financial Statements
topics.notes: Adjustments for prepayments, accruals, depreciation, bad and doubtful debts. Meaning and methods of depreciation (straight line and reducing balance).

topics.title: 10. Control Accounts
topics.notes: Meaning and preparation of Sales Ledger and Purchases Ledger Control Accounts.

topics.title: 11. Single Entry and Incomplete Records
topics.notes: Meaning, limitations, and preparation of final accounts from incomplete records.

topics.title: 12. Accounts of Not-For-Profit Organizations
topics.notes: Purpose, content, and preparation of Receipts and Payments Accounts, and Income and Expenditure Accounts.

topics.title: 13. Manufacturing Accounts
topics.notes: Meaning, purpose, terminologies, and preparation of Manufacturing, Trading, and Profit and Loss Accounts.

topics.title: 14. Partnership Accounts
topics.notes: Meaning and terms (partnership deed, drawings, interest on capital, interest on drawings); preparation of Capital and Current Accounts, Profit and Loss Appropriation Account, and Balance Sheet; admission of new partners and Goodwill Account.

topics.title: 15. Joint Venture Accounts
topics.notes: Meaning, purpose, and differences between joint venture and partnership.

topics.title: 16. Departmental and Branch Accounts
topics.notes: Importance, differences, and preparation of Departmental and simple Branch Accounts.

topics.title: 17. Introduction to Company Accounts
topics.notes: Formation, terminologies, and preparation of simple financial statements.

topics.title: 18. Interpretation of Accounts
topics.notes: Purpose and computation of financial ratios: net profit margin, stock turnover, quick ratio, acid test ratio, gross profit margin, and return on capital employed.

topics.title: 19. Purchase of Business
topics.notes: Reasons, terminologies, and preparation of accounts related to the purchase and sale of a business.

topics.title: 20. Consignment Accounts
topics.notes: Terminologies and preparation of simple Consignment Accounts.

topics.title: 21. Hire Purchase
topics.notes: Meaning and preparation of accounts in both seller's and hirer's books.

topics.title: 22. Contract Accounts
topics.notes: Meaning, purpose, terminologies, and preparation of Contract Accounts.

topics.title: 23. Cooperative Accounts
topics.notes: Meaning and objectives of cooperative societies.

note: Emphasis should be on practical application
references: F. Wood — Business Accounting Vol. 1 and 2
F.P. Langley — Introduction to Accounting for Business Studies
O.A. Longe and R.A. Kezeem — Essential Financial Accounting for Senior Secondary School
